solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Description of aural event very pleasant, mostly

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sound they heard as very nearly delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last letter from NICE, leaving NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic is the adjective for anything to do with sound, so it describes an event heard by the ear.

clue.text: After broadcasting sarcastic item I must ignore defamatory methods

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters the letters of the words sarcastic item, so they are rearranged
must ignore says the letter I is left out of the jumbled pool of letters

explanation.surface: A media story about a snide news piece that must be passed over as libel.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'After broadcasting' scrambles SARCASTIC ITEM, and 'must ignore' drops one I from those letters before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Smear tactics are ways of damaging a rival's reputation through slurs, which is exactly what defamatory methods are.

clue.text: Rather clever, providing opening for tourism in US city

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is the usual short form of New York
if means providing, as in 'providing it rains'

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of tourism

explanation.surface: A smart scheme to start up tourism in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for neat and clever, as in a nifty gadget or a nifty piece of footwork.

clue.text: Welcoming information in part of UK investing in fuel

indicators.note: investing means clothing or putting into, so the combined letters go inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel

indicators.note: in puts the slang word for information inside the abbreviation

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, one of the four parts of the United Kingdom
gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'

explanation.surface: Briefing on how one region of Britain is pouring money into its energy sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' reads like finance but means clothing: the fuel wraps NGENI (the information inside Northern Ireland, placed by 'in').
explanation.definitionFit: A congenial host or place is pleasant and friendly, which is what welcoming means.

clue.text: An atmosphere dismissing source of Italian style is rebellious

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dismissing sends a letter away from the word for atmosphere

parts.note: air means atmosphere, as in a place with an air of mystery

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: chic means style or elegance

explanation.surface: A fashion note: an elegant mood minus the Italian touch has turned defiant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes I, the first letter of Italian, from AIR to leave AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means lawless and refusing to accept authority, the attitude of a rebel.

clue.text: Shrewd, like student giving up English once

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

indicators.note: giving up means the student word surrenders one of its letters
once says the letter for English is dropped only one time, though the student word has two

parts.note: a tutee is a student being taught by a tutor

explanation.surface: A clever pupil, much like a learner who once abandoned English studies.
explanation.walkthrough: TUTEE has two Es; 'once' tells you to drop only one of them, leaving TUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and shrewd are close synonyms, both describing someone sharp at judging situations to their advantage.

clue.text: Rural river caught in tumult of Niagara

indicators.note: caught in places the single letter inside the jumbled waterfall name
a tumult is turmoil, so the letters of Niagara are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A river is swept into the roaring turbulence of Niagara Falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NIAGARA are rearranged into AGRAIAN, and R is caught inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian relates to farming and the land, so it is a near synonym of rural.

clue.text: Curl copper up round edge

indicators.note: round means the policeman's letters go around the word for edge
in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a copper is a police officer, abbreviated PC for police constable
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An instruction to bend a copper strip back up around its rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal (Cu) but is a policeman; 'up' gives CP, which 'round' puts either side of the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp hair is to press it into small waves or tight curls, so crimp works as a verb for curl.

clue.text: Anger when lines are busy for us after one

indicators.note: after says these pieces follow the numeral for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL means lines
a place that hums is busy and bustling with activity
our means belonging to us, for our use

explanation.surface: Temper flares when the phone lines are engaged and we wait after the first caller.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill humour is a bad mood or irritability, a milder form of anger.

clue.text: Provocative example of issue produced in Paris?

definitions.text: Provocative example of issue produced in Paris?

parts.words: Provocative example of issue produced in Paris?
parts.note: issue means offspring, so a French child who shocks people is a French phrase for an unruly young upstart

explanation.surface: Sounds like a debate about a controversial publication brought out in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' suggests a magazine edition, but here it means children; the French term for a shocking child names any daring maverick.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means terrible child and is used for someone whose unconventional behaviour provokes or embarrasses others.

clue.text: Places between flights on journey — this may be one

definitions.text: Places between flights on journey — this may be one

indicators.note: on puts the journey word next to the first piece in a down answer

parts.note: landings are the flat areas between flights of stairs
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: On a trip, the stopping points between flights are probably airfields.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an airstrip is a place used between flights on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is a runway where aircraft touch down, so it is a place between flights when travelling.

clue.text: Poet closing parts of number with very dodgy metres

indicators.note: the closing parts of words are their final letters, taken from three words in turn
dodgy means unreliable or shaky, so the letters of metres are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet ends a piece of verse with some very shaky metre.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'number with very' give RHY; 'dodgy' rearranges METRES into MESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of verse, usually a mediocre one, so the word is a slightly mocking term for a poet.

clue.text: University in China attracting a female

indicators.note: attracting means drawing the next letter onto the end of what came before
in places the university letter within the word for mate

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: An academic institution in China draws in a woman student.
explanation.walkthrough: China is capitalised to suggest the country, but in rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define first names simply by gender.

clue.text: Family employee showing a positive attitude

parts.note: up means upbeat or positive, as in feeling up
an air is a manner or attitude, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A household worker who displays an upbeat, cheerful outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreign person living with a family and helping with childcare in return for board.

clue.text: Items displayed by posters supporting this hobby

definitions.text: Items displayed by posters supporting this hobby

parts.words: Items displayed by posters supporting this hobby
parts.note: posters here are people posting letters, and the items on their envelopes are stamps, which collectors gather

explanation.surface: Sounds like wall posters advertising some pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posters' looks like printed placards, but means people who post letters; the stamps they stick on feed the collecting hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal name for stamp collecting, the hobby that depends on the postage stamps used on mail.

clue.text: Romantic approach and solemn promise that gives access to secrets?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: something which unlocks secrets

parts.note: to make a pass is to make a romantic or sexual advance
giving your word is making a solemn promise

explanation.surface: A seduction plus a sworn vow might win someone's confidences.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret code word typed or spoken to gain entry protects confidential information, so it unlocks secrets.

clue.text: Mum with annoyance missing year attending a mystical retreat

indicators.note: attending means accompanying, so the next letter goes alongside

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: missing means the year's letter is absent from the adverb

parts.note: angrily means with annoyance

explanation.surface: A mother, irritated about losing a year, goes off to a spiritual retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother but means keep quiet; 'missing' takes Y out of ANGRILY, giving ANGRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The name comes from the hidden Himalayan paradise of Lost Horizon, now used for any idyllic remote haven.

clue.text: Room provider keen to have Queen about to occupy bed

parts.note: hot means keen, as in hot on a subject

indicators.note: about means the royal letters go around the verb for staying in bed

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher
to lie is to occupy a bed

explanation.surface: An eager host makes up a bed for a royal guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the royal cipher round the verb, making ELIER; 'to have' simply joins it to the word for keen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotelier runs a hotel, the business that provides rooms for guests.

clue.text: A great many unwell in Eastern state, nursed by rather fewer

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside, as a baby is nursed in arms

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, which is rather fewer than the huge number being defined

indicators.note: in places the word for unwell inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a state in the eastern United States
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Many people fall ill in an eastern state, cared for by far fewer staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives RILLI, which 'nursed by' puts inside a hundred; 'rather fewer' is ironic understatement, since a hundred is vastly less than the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A number with twelve zeros stands for an enormous quantity, so informally it means a vast amount.

clue.text: Customer, old man, at marketplace

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
a tron is a Scottish word for a market place or public weighing beam

explanation.surface: Father goes shopping at the market, where he is a regular customer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tron is a Scottish name for a market place, where goods were weighed on a public beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular client of a shop, restaurant or business.

clue.text: Work on the Web to happen to involve arguments

indicators.note: involve means enclose, so the verb for happening goes around the quarrels

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place
rows are quarrels or arguments

explanation.surface: Going online seems certain to lead to heated disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look through web pages casually, so it describes using the internet.

clue.text: Millions chasing woman who does enchant

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the millions letter comes after the cleaner

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, a 'daily' who does for a household
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A woman pursued by riches is someone who casts spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who does' is the old British phrase for a cleaner who 'does' for a family; the char's letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm is to delight or captivate, the same as enchanting someone.

clue.text: American inventor leaving small item unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a morsel is a small piece or item, especially of food

explanation.surface: A US inventor walks off leaving a tiny piece of work incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Morse invented the telegraph code named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Morse was the American who developed the electric telegraph and its dot-dash code.

clue.text: Say nothing adopted by sort of professor is outrageous

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

indicators.note: adopted by means taken inside the professor word

parts.note: a Regius professor holds a chair founded by the Crown at an old British university
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Saying nothing, as a certain kind of professor does, is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: A Regius professor holds a royally founded chair at Oxford, Cambridge or a Scottish university.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means shockingly bad or flagrant, the same as outrageous.

clue.text: Big figures try to pick up a lot of support

indicators.note: in a down clue picking up raises the letters, so they read upwards

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm

explanation.surface: Weightlifters attempt to lift a great deal of the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are giants of folklore, so they are huge figures.

clue.text: Bring up opinion by newspaper: motorist looks into it

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: the thing a driver glances into

parts.note: to rear is to bring up children
a view is an opinion
the Mirror is a British daily tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Raising a point of view in a tabloid while a driver checks behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers glance into this glass above the windscreen to see traffic behind them.

clue.text: Crikey — it's just like 1984

definitions.meaning: the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four was written ... Orwell, so the book is the work of a writer called George

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in alarm that things have become as dystopian as the novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 1984 is not a year here but Orwell's novel, whose author's real first name was Eric but pen name George.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation of surprise, and literally the authorship of Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Story-teller recalled river meeting larger body of water

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: the Po is the main river of northern Italy
a sea is a larger body of water than a river

explanation.surface: A narrator remembers where a river flowed into the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses POSEA to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables such as The Tortoise and the Hare.
